picks.why: the fortified Great Synagogue, a major Lutsk landmark; clean, sharp engraving

picks.what: Lubart’s Castle, book illustration (Stefan Szyller, Czy mamy polską architekturę?)
picks.why: the castle’s gate and Styr towers, the city’s defining landmark; book page and caption trimmed

gaps: P0: only pages of the Lutsk Gospel; P1–P3: nothing; P6: existing 2014 castle and cathedral view kept
notes: #11 is dated by the book’s 1916 publication; the photo itself may be a few years older. The trim keeps 57% of the page width (about 2,500 px), which is the photo itself. #8 (colored postcard of the Bratskyi Bridge square with the Orthodox Brotherhood church, 1910s, German and Polish caption so probably 1915–18) is an alternate for P5 but is a busy market scene. #9 and #10 are small portrait-format cards of the castle tower. #4 (Bernardine church) has only a “19th century” date. #7 (synagogue photo, 1910) is 38 years after #6 and shows the same building.
